message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I'm p1 with $2364 on ST_JAMES_PLACE. I own a brown monopoly with one house, a pink monopoly at four houses, and an orange monopoly at four houses. Most other properties are mortgaged.

p2 is in jail with only $110 and everything mortgaged. They cannot unmortgage the reds because it costs roughly $374. p3 and p4 are bankrupt. The bank now has just 7 houses left.

p2 sold houses on the reds, returning them to the bank. Building hotels would cost $100 each and return four houses per property to the bank.

Hoteling would flood the bank with houses, but p2 cannot use them. Even if they pay to get out of jail and collect $200 from passing GO, they still lack the cash to unmortgage the reds or build.

I am calculating exact rent increases from hotels. Orange properties would jump from $800 to $1000 per house. Pink properties would rise from roughly $750–$900 to $950–$1100. I need to verify these standard US Monopoly values before deciding.

Standard rent values are now confirmed. New York Avenue with four houses pays $800 and a hotel pays $1000. Virginia Avenue with four houses pays $700 and a hotel pays $900. St. Charles and States Avenue with four houses pay $625 each and a hotel pays $750. Each hotel costs $100.

I have enough cash to build six hotels for $600. The bank has twelve hotels available, so this is feasible.

The real question is whether it matters. p2 cannot pay any rent above $110. Even a $625 hit on St. Charles Place would bankrupt them immediately. They have no houses left to sell and no mortgage liquidity. Hoteling these properties would not change the outcome.

The housing lock is already broken. p2 cannot buy the seven houses the bank now holds. Hoteling would return those houses to the bank, but p2 is already bankrupt and cannot rebuild.

I am now considering buying the remaining houses to lock the bank again. The brown properties have only one house each, so I can even them out with the two brown spaces. Mediterranean has zero houses and Baltic has one. Building on brown costs only $50 per house, which is cheap but yields little rent. I could sink all seven available houses into the browns to deny p2 any future building options.

I can even the brown properties by adding seven houses to the browns, exactly matching the bank's seven available houses. This would cost $350 and leave me with $2014. I need to verify whether the engine requires even distribution at every step or only at the end.

I will build four houses on Mediterranean Avenue and three on Baltic Avenue. This ends with both browns at four houses, satisfying the even distribution requirement.

I will build incrementally instead of all at once. Adding one house to Mediterranean Avenue first matches Baltic Avenue's single house. This keeps the distribution even and avoids engine validation issues.

The greens are split between us, so I cannot block p2 from building there. They own Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois mortgaged, which would form a red monopoly if unmortgaged, but that would cost $374 total.

p2 cannot afford to unmortgage the reds this turn. Even after collecting $200 from passing GO, they would still be $64 short of the $374 needed. They would need multiple passes or a cash card before they could build there.

This makes the housing lock less critical. Still, spending $350 on the browns is cheap insurance. It also raises rent slightly if p2 lands on those spaces.

I will not hotel the properties. Returning four houses per property to the bank would give p2 a chance to rebuild if they ever collect enough cash.

Unmortgaging is unnecessary. I will keep my green properties unmortgaged and do not need to trade them.

Even a lucky $510 windfall from Community Chest and GO would still leave p2 $136 short of the $150 needed to buy a house. The housing lock is therefore unnecessary insurance. I will build one house on Mediterranean Avenue.
